$schema_note: Hand-curated record of what ForgePact's boss soul pieces (ForgePact#197) rely on, NOT mechanically extracted (see hs-game-sdk/curated/satanic_zone.json for why curated/ exists). Data only: no binding is generated from this file, and hs_game_sdk/soul_piece_model.py never reads it; tests/test_soul_piece_model.py reads both, checks the shared `cases` against the model and its own transforms of ForgePact's code, and (ParityTests, where ForgePact is checked out) pins ForgePact/plugin/include/ForgePact/SoulPieceMod.hpp's constants, seeds, base, act table with boss rooms, portal offset, room rules and verdict words to this file. The mechanism, in our own words, is docs/models/soul-piece-spec.md; the game facts are docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md § 21 and § 18.4; the act of each room is hs-game-sdk/curated/room_acts.json. A `status` is one of `static_reading` (read from the compiled game and paraphrased, no script text), `inference` (follows from static readings, not read directly), `owner_named` (the owner's decision, not a reading), `our_code` (ForgePact's own choice), `measured` (a live session read it; `capture` names the session's capture, a local file the hub does not track), `unverified` (a plausible value no session has read) or `pending` (a live check of ForgePact#197 fills it). A `source` is `<path> § <section>`, the path relative to the hub root and the section text appearing in that file. `seed_base` + act is a piece's seed `a`; `reserved_seeds` are other ForgePact items' seeds a piece must never take. `base` is the game item a piece is made of: the repository entry of that name in that category, resolved by name at run time, of that class, `c` and `j`. `gem` is the Gem of Incarnation whose `droprate.base` G ForgePact reads at run time by repository name; `ratio` makes the piece's denominator D = max(1, floor(G x numerator / denominator)), 0 (no piece) for G unknown, zero or negative. `acts` is one row per act: the boss object its room is expected to bring out (an hs_game_sdk object name, with the SDK's index), the piece's name, the act's boss room (an hs_game_sdk room name, with the SDK's index) where a piece's portal leads, `named` (false would make the act drop nothing and open no portal) and the row's evidence. `portal` is where the portal stands and what it is. `room_rules` are the name rules that refuse a room on top of the act table, each with the verdict word it gives. `drop_verdicts` and `use_verdicts` are the words, in the order ForgePact asks them; `force_overrides` the drop verdicts `soulpiece force on` may replace with `hit`. `cases` are shared inputs and their expected answer: `drop` (DecideDrop; `act` is the room's act, 0 for none) and `use` (DecideUse; `act` is the room's act, 0 for none, and a `portal` case names the boss room it leads to) are ForgePact's; `stack` is the game's stack rule (soul_piece_model.stacks) for an item `picked` up beside a `held` one, each `{t: class, b, c, a: seed}`, where a `b` other than the base's 12 stands for any definition of that class. A roll is uniform in [0, 1). `open_questions` are the questions about the game Live procedure 3 answers (and the ones no session can), each with the live check that answers it and the model's HYPOTHESES key where it decides one.

portal.source: docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md § 21.5 Portals and travel between rooms
portal.note: The portal stands 96 px to the player's right, mirrored to the left past the room's width, at the player's y (Live procedure 1: 1200 px to the side was off-screen). Its target is the act's boss room, written into the record its portalZone key names; the game's own travel takes the player there, and the room's Pentagram_Boss_obj brings out the boss.

room_rules.note: A room drops pieces when RoomActIndex gives it an act and no rule refuses it; towns refuse first, then the boss-room rules. A use opens its portal in any room with an act, towns included, and is refused (the piece kept) in a room with no act and by the boss-room rules.

use_rules.action: right-click the piece in the backpack and confirm
use_rules.note: Every verdict but portal is a refusal: PotionUse answers false and the game keeps the piece. On portal the portal opens, PotionUse answers true and the game clears the piece's cell itself, as it does for the Edible PAS Logo.
